question: In visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), a positive result is indicated by the appearance of a well-defined acetowhite area within or abutting the transformation zone of the cervix.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is true. VIA uses 3–5% acetic acid; abnormal cells with high nuclear density turn white (acetowhite), constituting a positive result. Lugol's iodine is used in VILI, not VIA.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A VIA-positive result is defined by a well-defined, dense acetowhite area close to or touching the squamocolumnar junction. Indistinct or pale whitening is not considered positive.
